name: each call has its own parameters: one read after the call of its own name
source: const sum = (n: int): int => n == 0 ? 0 : sum(n - 1) + n; sum(4)

name: each call has its own parameters: a lambda inside reads those of its own call
source: const f = (n: int): int => n == 0 ? 0 : [1].map(x => f(n - 1) + n)[0]; f(3)

name: each call has its own const names
source: const f = (n: int): int => { const m = n * 2; n <= 0 ? 0 : f(n - 1) + m }; f(3)

name: each call has its own pattern names
source: const f = ({n, s}: {n: int, s: string}): string => n <= 0 ? s : f({n: n - 1, s: s + "a"}) + s; f({n: 2, s: "x"})

name: each call has its own defaults
source: const f = (n: int, acc: int = n * 10): int => n <= 0 ? acc : f(n - 1) + acc; f(2)

name: each call has its own name of catch
source: const f = (n: int): string => try { fail(`e${n}`) } catch (e) { n <= 0 ? e.message : f(n - 1) + e.message }; f(2)

name: a parameter read after a failure unwound deeper calls

name: fib
source: const fib = (n: int): int => n < 2 ? n : fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2); fib(10)
